characteristic_features: presents with perforation, obstruction, or refractory celiac symptoms

biomarkers.name: HLA-DQ2 / HLA-DQ8 (celiac genotype)
biomarkers.prevalence: Common in EATL (celiac-associated), reflecting underlying celiac disease; not specific as a lymphoma biomarker
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports celiac association in EATL; not by itself sufficient to distinguish EATL from MEITL

biomarkers.name: CD30
biomarkers.clinical_use: May support consideration of brentuximab vedotin in CD30+ cases

biomarkers.name: CD8+/CD56- (EATL) vs CD8+/CD56+ (MEITL)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish EATL from MEITL; classic EATL is often CD8- and CD56-, whereas MEITL is typically CD8+ and CD56+

biomarkers.name: STAT5B mutations (MEITL)
biomarkers.clinical_use: MEITL molecular characterization; supports JAK/STAT pathway involvement

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Intraepithelial T-cell infiltrate expanding into pleomorphic lymphoma with associated enteropathy (villous atrophy, intraepithelial lymphocytosis)
variants: classic EATL (celiac-associated, HLA-DQ2/DQ8-associated, typically CD56-, often CD8-)
MEITL — monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal TCL (not celiac-associated, typically CD8+/CD56+, more common in East Asia)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: EATL emerges from long-standing celiac disease and refractory celiac disease type II; JAK/STAT pathway activation is implicated in both EATL and MEITL
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Villous atrophy and intraepithelial lymphocytosis in surrounding mucosa (celiac features); often multifocal small bowel involvement

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) of small intestinal mucosa
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm — lymphoid (intraepithelial cytotoxic T cells of intestinal mucosa)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Cytotoxic T-cell differentiation with intraepithelial phenotype (CD103+, TIA-1+, granzyme B+); classic EATL is usually CD56- and often CD8-; MEITL is typically CD56+ and CD8+
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Two distinct entities: classic EATL emerges from refractory celiac disease type II (RCDII) — chronic gluten-driven IEL clonal expansion → lymphomagenesis with IL-15/JAK-STAT pathway biology; MEITL (monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma) is a distinct entity not celiac-associated with recurrent STAT5B, JAK3, GNAI2, and SETD2 alterations
